title: Drone orthomosaic segmentation across new farms
prompt: We need to segment individual olive-tree crowns from RGB drone orthomosaics. We have 18 orthomosaics from six farms, with three flights per farm collected on nearby dates. Ground sampling distance ranges from 2.1 to 3.4 cm. Crown polygons were drawn on the completed orthomosaics. The current proposal creates overlapping 512 x 512 tiles, randomly assigns tiles to 70% training, 15% validation and 15% test, computes normalization statistics from all tiles, selects the best model on test IoU, and reports the tile-level bootstrap confidence interval. The intended deployment is on previously unseen farms in another region during the following growing season. We have enough budget to annotate two additional orthomosaics, but no new-region labels are currently available. Review the proposal and give a concrete dataset, split, training, evaluation and evidence plan. Do not browse the web. Use only the supplied facts and clearly identify information that must be measured or decided rather than inventing values.
criticalFailures: Accepts random allocation of overlapping tiles as evidence for unseen-farm or new-region deployment.
Allows normalization, model selection or other fitted decisions to use the final test data.
Treats tile-level resampling as an independent uncertainty analysis when inference concerns farms or orthomosaics.
Invents a buffer distance, IoU threshold, sample size or acceptance criterion without project evidence or a stated requirement.

criteria.description: Connects the split and evidence design to deployment on unseen farms, a new region and a later season, while distinguishing what the current six farms can and cannot establish.

Keeps overlapping tiles, flights and products from the same farm or source orthomosaic in appropriate groups and identifies orthomosaic construction and neighboring content as dependence or leakage risks.
Fits normalization and tunes preprocessing, augmentation, architecture and thresholds using training and development data only, preserving an untouched final evaluation role.
Checks polygon quality, boundary ambiguity, resolution variation, crown support, tiling edge effects and the consequences of resampling or scale normalization.

Uses task-appropriate object and/or segmentation evidence at meaningful geographic support and treats farm or orthomosaic units, rather than tiles alone, as the uncertainty unit when justified by the target population.

Uses the two-orthomosaic annotation budget to resolve a material evidence gap, records the split and preprocessing lineage needed for reproduction, and explains the limitation if no representative new-region evaluation can be obtained.

title: SAR ship detection under geographic and acquisition shift
prompt: We are designing a ship detector from Sentinel-1 IW GRD scenes with VV and VH channels. The archive contains 420 scenes from 30 ports over four years, with repeated relative orbits and many adjacent acquisitions. Candidate ship labels come from AIS positions matched within a time window, but the matching error and missing-AIS rate have not been quantified. The proposed pipeline clips the backscatter to a visually chosen range, converts each channel to 8-bit PNG, duplicates VV into three channels for an ImageNet detector, randomly splits 256 x 256 patches, and reports patch mAP. Deployment will cover ports and open-water routes in countries absent from training, including different incidence-angle distributions and sea states. Review the measurement, label, dataset, preprocessing, modeling and validation plan. Recommend the simplest defensible baseline and the next comparison only if a named limitation justifies it. Do not browse the web or invent numeric thresholds.
criticalFailures: Treats GRD backscatter as ordinary RGB imagery without checking calibration, units, geometry, incidence angle, polarization and product preprocessing.
Accepts random patch splitting despite repeated ports, orbits, dates or adjacent acquisitions.
Treats AIS-derived labels as complete and exact without addressing temporal matching, positional uncertainty and missing transmissions.
Claims geographic transfer from a patch-level in-distribution test.

criteria.description: Defines and preserves the GRD measurement contract, including calibration state, units or scale, geometry, polarization, incidence-angle effects, speckle and NoData or land masking; questions irreversible visual clipping and 8-bit conversion; and treats RGB-pretrained adaptation as a controlled candidate rather than a default truth.
Characterizes AIS matching uncertainty, missing positives, non-ship confounders and the spatial-temporal support of labels, with a targeted review strategy.
Groups dependent patches by appropriate scene, acquisition, port, orbit and time units and reserves evidence that reflects absent countries, open-water routes and acquisition shift.
Defines a modest reproducible detector baseline and adds a more specialized architecture, pretraining scheme or adaptation method only for an observed material limitation.
Evaluates detection at scene and deployment-relevant support, includes false alarms and missed ships across relevant strata, and calibrates any operating threshold on development evidence only.
Records scene and label lineage, preprocessing and split configuration, and identifies the external evidence still required for the claimed deployment population.

title: Multimodal land-change mapping for future events
prompt: A team wants to map post-fire vegetation loss for future wildfire events. Available training data cover 24 fires from 2019-2024. Inputs include pre-fire and post-fire Sentinel-2 surface-reflectance composites, Sentinel-1 GRD VV/VH composites and annual 10 m embedding products. Fire-severity polygons were interpreted mainly from the same post-fire optical imagery. The current proposal resamples every input to a common 10 m grid, concatenates all channels, randomly splits pixels, fine-tunes the largest available foundation model, selects the probability threshold on the test set and reports overall pixel accuracy. Intended deployment is on fires from 2026 onward across ecosystems and countries absent from training, with cloudy optical observations sometimes unavailable. Review the problem formulation and propose a defensible end-to-end strategy covering target construction, temporal availability, alignment, fusion, baselines, splitting, missing modalities, validation, uncertainty and deployment. Do not browse the web. Do not assume that a named embedding or foundation model is suitable without establishing its input and temporal contract.
criticalFailures: Accepts random pixel splitting across the same fire events.
Uses information that would not be available at the declared prediction time or ignores possible temporal leakage from annual embeddings.
Assumes that resampling to the same nominal grid proves physical or semantic alignment.
Selects thresholds or models on the final test set or claims future-country generalization from the current random split.

criteria.description: Defines the prediction time, target meaning and support, distinguishes vegetation loss from fire severity where necessary, and examines circularity from labels interpreted from the same optical evidence.
Checks sensor processing, units, dates, compositing, embedding vintage and provenance, and whether every input would be available for a future event at inference time.
Verifies CRS, transforms, support, resolution, resampling semantics and co-registration, then chooses a fusion strategy that acknowledges modality and temporal differences.
Groups samples by fire event and constructs development and final evidence around future events, unseen ecosystems or countries, while stating what 24 historical fires cannot establish.

Starts with interpretable sensor-matched baselines and evaluates embeddings or foundation models only after verifying bands, temporal coverage, normalization, resolution, weights, license and software contract.
Plans for cloudy or absent optical data without silently changing the deployment population and distinguishes confidence, calibration, out-of-distribution evidence and abstention.
Uses event-level and map-relevant metrics, development-only thresholding, stratified diagnostics and recorded data, split, preprocessing and model configurations.

title: Change detection from single-date supervision under domain shift
prompt: A remote-sensing team needs a binary change detector for bi-temporal optical imagery, but it has very few labelled image pairs. It has a much larger collection of single-date images with pixel-level land-cover annotations, access to general pretrained image models, and the capacity to generate or edit training imagery if that is justified. Deployment will be on regions and imaging conditions absent from development data. Design the target, supervision, model-development and evaluation strategy. Decide whether and how single-date annotations, pretraining and synthetic data should be used; define the comparisons needed to determine whether each adds real-domain value; and state what evidence would support a domain-generalization claim. Do not browse the web, inspect local files other than benchmark-provided skill instructions, search for a matching publication, name a remembered paper, or invent performance values.
criticalFailures: Treats random pairing of unrelated single-date images as a realistic model of geographic change without testing spatial, semantic and radiometric artifacts.
Uses target-domain labels, validation data or test results to tune a method presented as zero-shot domain generalization.
Assumes generated imagery preserves remote-sensing geometry, radiometry and class semantics without quality controls or real-pair validation.
Claims that generic pretraining or synthetic supervision establishes target-domain performance without an untouched real-domain evaluation.

criteria.description: Defines the change target, prediction support, available single-date supervision, inference-time inputs and the intended unseen-domain claim.

Defines defensible uses of scarce paired labels, single-date semantic labels and optional synthetic supervision while preserving spatial correspondence and the distinction between real change and nuisance variation.
Explains how temporal correspondence and dense pixel or object support are modeled, and treats pretrained representations as hypotheses whose suitability and adaptation must be tested.
Compares the simplest paired-data baseline with single-date, pretrained and synthetic alternatives using controlled ablations that can attribute any target-domain change.

Keeps target-domain labels and results outside development, evaluates multiple untouched real domains with change-sensitive metrics and relevant nuisance strata, audits synthetic shortcuts, and limits claims to the observed transfer conditions.

title: Fine-grained cropland change under phenological and boundary interference
prompt: Design a binary cropland change detector for pairs of high-resolution optical images assembled from different acquisition dates and, in some evaluation regions, different image sources. Unchanged fields may have strong seasonal, illumination or management differences; cropland can resemble forest, grassland, water or bare soil; and true changes may be small, fragmented, narrow or irregular. Orthorectification and CRS metadata are available, but residual image and label displacement has not been quantified. Propose an end-to-end measurement, data, model and evaluation strategy. Explain how the design separates real conversion from nuisance variation, preserves small-region and boundary evidence, and tests geographic and seasonal transfer without assuming that a more complex architecture is necessary. Do not browse the web, inspect local files other than benchmark-provided skill instructions, search for a matching publication, name a remembered paper, or invent thresholds or results.
criticalFailures: Treats matching CRS or nominal pixel size as proof of physical co-registration, or assumes feature-space alignment can repair unmeasured source displacement.
Responds only with a larger backbone or foundation model without addressing nuisance change, fine spatial support and label uncertainty.
Claims generalization from in-dataset patch scores or unlabelled visual examples alone.
Invents boundary tolerances, patch-size thresholds or acceptance criteria without data or operational justification.

criteria.description: Audits source products, CRS, transforms, resolution, acquisition geometry and dates; measures residual image and label displacement; and keeps physical co-registration distinct from learned feature alignment.
Defines cropland conversion and its label support, separates phenology, illumination, management and background similarity from the target, and accounts for annotation uncertainty.
Uses complementary temporal and spatial evidence to discriminate real conversion from nuisance variation while retaining responses for small and fragmented changes.
Preserves multiscale region and boundary information with a justified decoder or post-processing design and does not confuse neural feature refinement with physical registration.
Starts with credible early- or late-fusion and simple difference baselines, then adds complexity only for observed failure modes and isolates each material change.
Uses region and boundary evidence at spatially independent support, reports efficiency and stability, and requires labelled held-out geographic or seasonal evaluation for transfer claims.

title: Multimodal 3D building change with metric height information
prompt: A 3D building-change system receives a pre-event digital surface model and a later nominally co-registered optical orthophoto. Training datasets also provide semantic building-change labels and continuous height-change maps derived from independent elevation observations, but their acquisition method, vertical datum, uncertainty and masking rules vary by dataset and must be audited. The deployed system must produce both a semantic change map and a per-pixel height-change estimate. Small vertical differences are common and may be near measurement or registration uncertainty, while large structural changes are rare but operationally important. Design the measurement audit, baselines, multimodal model, training and validation strategy without assuming a particular fusion architecture. Address cross-city generalization and computational cost. Do not browse the web, inspect local files other than benchmark-provided skill instructions, search for a matching publication, name a remembered paper, or invent thresholds or results.
criticalFailures: Discards DSM metric meaning or applies generic image scaling without auditing units, vertical datum, target provenance, noise and co-registration; using a DSM raster channel as a controlled baseline is not itself a failure.
Derives a universal building-change threshold from DSM accuracy or an invented height value without validation against the operational target.
Uses only semantic accuracy or only height RMSE and ignores the joint output contract and changed-region behavior.
Claims cross-city transfer using only random patches or cities represented during development.

criteria.description: Preserves input and target units and provenance, verifies CRS, resolution, vertical datum, temporal meaning, masks and co-registration, and distinguishes sensor accuracy from detectable building change.
Compares optical-only, DSM-only and simple multimodal baselines while preserving metric elevation semantics, then diagnoses whether modality-specific processing is needed.
Chooses fusion and feature specialization according to demonstrated baseline failures, controls added complexity, and does not assume that routed experts or handcrafted priors are necessary.

Models semantic change and continuous height variation as related but distinct targets, audits their consistency, and addresses long-tailed magnitudes without suppressing uncertain small changes by fiat.

Uses semantic, boundary and metric-height errors including changed-region errors, repeated-run stability, measurement uncertainty, error analysis by change magnitude and controlled component ablations.
Evaluates held-out cities or morphologies, reports compute and memory costs, and limits transfer claims to the observed geographic and sensor range.

title: Subpixel standing-dead-tree detectability from satellite imagery
prompt: A multi-region forest study has 3 m multispectral surface-reflectance imagery and much finer UAV polygons for standing dead trees and competing land-cover classes. UAV annotation covers only part of some satellite pixels, individual pixels contain mixtures, isolated targets can occupy only a fraction of a pixel, and residual image-to-label displacement may remain. The objective is to determine when the satellite signal is detectable and reliable, not merely to maximize a segmentation score. Design the measurement checks, label representation, data lifecycle, models, probability analysis and scale-dependent validation. Distinguish exploratory characterization of response transitions from selection and independent confirmation of an operational threshold. Do not browse the web, inspect local files other than benchmark-provided skill instructions, search for a matching publication, name a remembered paper, or invent detectability boundaries.
criticalFailures: Splits overlapping tiles randomly instead of keeping every site and its derived tiles within one partition.
Rasterizes UAV polygons as complete hard labels while treating unknown or uncovered fractions as confirmed background and ignoring mixed-pixel composition.
Selects an operational threshold on the final test set, reports a descriptive transition as independently validated, or universalizes it without external confirmation.
Reports only overall pixel accuracy or one model's best F1 and does not analyse probability response across spatial support and background conditions.

criteria.description: Preserves reflectance scaling and acquisition metadata, verifies alignment, represents residual displacement as uncertainty, and measures annotated and unknown coverage at satellite support.

Represents annotated class fractions and unknown coverage separately, uses hard or soft targets only within their support, validates any confidence weighting, and does not convert unlabelled area to background.

Partitions by independent site before tiling, balances relevant factors using development data, estimates any operating rule without the final test set, and reserves independent sites for confirmation.

Uses a transparent spectral baseline and suitable spatial models, analyses continuous probabilities, validates calibration and threshold sensitivity, and tests whether response patterns persist across architectures.
Relates responses to fractional target cover, surrounding spatial support, aggregation or connected extent, and competing background composition at prespecified meaningful supports.

Reports support counts and uncertainty, separates descriptive from confirmatory thresholds, tests consistency across models and regions, and limits global or individual-tree claims under geographic imbalance and alignment uncertainty.
